name: io.github.zz-plant/whether
title: Whether
description: This week's call on startup hiring, fundraising and burn, from U.S. rates and credit data.

tools.name: get_state
tools.description: This week's call on startup hiring, spending, fundraising and burn, read from U.S. interest-rate and credit-market data and published every Monday. Use it when someone asks whether to hire or freeze hiring, raise now or wait, cut burn, or what today's funding or macro conditions mean for their company. The smallest answer to decide from, about 3KB: the conditions and the margin from their change lines, each score against its pause, restart and change lines, the moves behind each score since the earlier reading, the areas those moves crossed a line for, the guidance, and the data's freshness. automation.ready is false when the reading is a saved copy or more than 10 days old.

tools.name: get_brief
tools.description: The full brief (about 22KB): summary prose, decision delta, flip watch, provenance and the agent handoff, for a cadence. Use get_state when you only need to decide; use week (e.g. '2026-w41') or period (e.g. '2024-q1') to retrieve frozen historical records.

week.description: A specific published week slug (e.g. '2026-w41') to fetch that frozen record.

period.description: A specific archive period slug (e.g. '2024-q1' or '2023') to fetch that frozen posture record.

tools.name: get_changes_since
tools.description: Whether the published weekly call changed since a week you name (e.g. '2026-w41'): the conditions and each area's pause or restart state, compared week by week from the frozen records, never from wording. For an agent that runs on a schedule and acts only on a change: pass the nextSince this returned last time. Without since, the newest eight weeks.

since.description: A published week slug, e.g. '2026-w41'. The comparison starts from the last week published at or before it.

tools.name: get_answer
tools.description: Whether's answer to one startup operating question, with this week's standing, the rules in force and a line to cite: hiring or a hiring freeze, engineers, sales headcount or a first salesperson, layoffs, compensation, raising capital or a bridge round, runway before a raise, cutting burn, vendors, pricing, retention versus acquisition, the roadmap, new product lines, go-to-market pace, international expansion, preparing for a downturn, a board or executive briefing, the funding climate, or risk-on versus risk-off. Pass the question as the user asked it. A refusal says where to go next, often stress_test_plan.

question.description: The question in the user's words, a topic, or an answer slug (e.g. 'should I hire a second engineer', 'cut burn', 'should-we-freeze-or-selectively-hire').

tools.name: get_standup_line
tools.description: Returns the daily standup one-liner stating guidance movement this week and the conditions that would change it.

tools.name: get_decision_rules
tools.description: The bounded rules behind the guidance: for each operating area, the action, the line that pauses it and the trigger that reverses it. Keyed by regime; one regime, or all four when none is given. The rules are the same every week; get_state says where today's scores sit against the lines.

regime.description: A regime by key (SCARCITY, DEFENSIVE, VOLATILE, EXPANSION) or by the word the site prints (Freezing, Cloudy, Stormy, Sunny), in any case. Omit for all four.

tools.name: get_context
tools.description: How long a regime has lasted, how long its past runs lasted, and what most often came next, in months of month-end snapshots up to `latestSnapshot`. Defaults to today's conditions; `inputs` says which values were yours and which were today's.

regime.description: A regime by key (SCARCITY, DEFENSIVE, VOLATILE, EXPANSION) or by the word the site prints (Freezing, Cloudy, Stormy, Sunny), in any case. Defaults to today's conditions.

tools.name: get_projection
tools.description: Weeks until the scores cross a line where conditions change at a given pace, and the regime they would then be in. A score moving away from its line will not cross it. With no arguments it uses today's scores and their pace; give scores to ask what-if, and any pace you leave out is taken as 0. `inputs` says which values were yours, which were today's, and which were assumed.

regime.description: A regime by key (SCARCITY, DEFENSIVE, VOLATILE, EXPANSION) or by the word the site prints (Freezing, Cloudy, Stormy, Sunny), in any case. Defaults to today's conditions. The projection runs from where the scores sit; the result says so when they sit in another regime.

tightness.description: Funding pressure, 0 to 100. Defaults to today's.

riskAppetite.description: Risk appetite, 0 to 100. Defaults to today's.

tightnessDelta.description: Funding pressure's pace in points per week, not the total change since an earlier reading. Defaults to today's pace when no score is given, else 0.

riskAppetiteDelta.description: Risk appetite's pace in points per week, not the total change since an earlier reading. Defaults to today's pace when no score is given, else 0.

tools.name: get_comps
tools.description: Median SaaS EV/Revenue multiple across 14 public companies, from SEC filings and delayed prices, or Yahoo Finance when those are down; the result names its source. Use it when someone asks what public SaaS companies trade at. Fails with each source's reason when none answers.

tools.name: get_signals
tools.description: Which years and months the historical record covers.

tools.name: get_recent_history
tools.description: The trailing 92-day window for one signal from the materialized model, for temporal analysis without parsing the whole brief.

signal_key.description: One of TREASURY_1M, TREASURY_3M, TREASURY_2Y, TREASURY_10Y, BBB_CREDIT_SPREAD, HY_CREDIT_SPREAD, CPI_YOY, UNEMPLOYMENT_RATE, CHICAGO_FCI, VIX_INDEX, in any case.

tools.name: stress_test_plan
tools.description: Audits a proposed operational decision (hiring, cloud commit, office lease, vendor deal or discount) against today's funding pressure and risk appetite, and returns the fragile assumptions, the pause line and the restart line. A plan it has no rules for comes back with a null verdict and where to look instead; pass `category` if you know which kind of decision it is. Pass the company's figures to size it. A plan naming several commitments returns each one in `commitments`, graded and sized on its own, and the verdict covers them together. Use it when someone describes a specific plan and asks whether it holds up in this market.

planText.description: The planned decision or initiative in plain English.

lifecycle.description: Company lifecycle stage; defaults to GROWTH.

category.description: The kind of decision, when the plan's wording doesn't name one the test has rules for.

cashUsd.description: Cash in the bank, in dollars. Sizes the plan against it.

monthlySpendUsd.description: Total monthly spend, in dollars, before revenue.

runwayMonths.description: Months of runway, when you don't have cash and spend to work it out from.

tools.name: lint_commitment
tools.description: Scans an engineering PRD, RFC or contract for fixed capital lock-in (multi-year reservations, large upfront cash commitments) and offers reversible alternatives, against today's conditions.

specText.description: The PRD, RFC, or procurement specification text.

category.description: The kind of decision, when the plan's wording doesn't name one the test has rules for.

cashUsd.description: Cash in the bank, in dollars. Sizes the plan against it.

monthlySpendUsd.description: Total monthly spend, in dollars, before revenue.

runwayMonths.description: Months of runway, when you don't have cash and spend to work it out from.

tools.name: lint_sprint_goal
tools.description: Takes a sprint goal or story-level plan and says whether it holds, pauses, or needs a written way to undo it under today's conditions, with the pause line that would fire; `not_graded` when the test has no rules for it. A sprint goal is a planned decision at smaller granularity, so this reuses the stress-test engine.

goalText.description: The sprint goal or story-level plan in plain English.

lifecycle.description: Company lifecycle stage; defaults to GROWTH.

category.description: The kind of decision, when the plan's wording doesn't name one the test has rules for.

cashUsd.description: Cash in the bank, in dollars. Sizes the plan against it.

monthlySpendUsd.description: Total monthly spend, in dollars, before revenue.

runwayMonths.description: Months of runway, when you don't have cash and spend to work it out from.

tools.name: audit_sprint_retro
tools.description: Audits a sprint's recorded commitments against today's bounded pause triggers to surface retro violations (e.g. net-new hiring or platform rewrites committed while pause lines are active).

planText.description: A planned decision or commitment to evaluate against pause lines.

lifecycle.description: Company lifecycle stage; defaults to GROWTH.

tools.name: get_analog_playbook
tools.description: Matches today's conditions against four hand-picked past periods (Q3 2007, Q4 2018, Q2 2021, Q2 2022) and returns, for the closest, the common mistake then, the move that held up, and the sign that marked the turn. Editorial summaries of the public record, not a measured sample of companies.

tools.name: list_agent_skills
tools.description: The skill ids and output order an agent runtime should follow when working from a Whether brief.
